title: Pumping and Storing Breast Milk
hook: Expressing milk lets someone else share feeds and keeps supply going when you're back at work. The trick is a simple storage rule — and gentle handling so the milk stays good for baby.
key_points: A handy storage rule of thumb: about 4 hours at room temperature, 4 days in the fridge, and up to 6 months (best) in the freezer.
Label each container with the date and use the oldest milk first; store in small amounts to avoid waste.
Thaw in the fridge or under warm water — never the microwave, which creates hot spots; swirl (don't shake) and don't refreeze thawed milk.
Wash hands before pumping and clean all pump parts after each use; expressing also helps maintain supply when returning to work.
content_html: For many families, expressing milk is what makes breastfeeding work alongside the rest of life — it lets a partner or caregiver take a feed, builds a small stash, and helps keep supply up when you head back to work. You can express by hand or with a manual or electric pump; whatever the method, washing your hands first and cleaning the pump parts after each use keeps the milk safe.
extra_html: Storage is mostly about a simple rule of thumb: roughly four hours at room temperature, four days in the fridge, and up to about six months — ideally — in the freezer. Store milk in small portions so you thaw only what you need, and label every container with the date so you can use the oldest first. When it's time to use it, thaw in the fridge or under warm running water rather than the microwave, which heats unevenly and can scald a baby. Swirl the milk gently to mix the layers instead of shaking it, and don't refreeze milk that's already been thawed. This is general guidance — the CDC and your lactation supporter have detailed charts if you want exact times.

related.title: Breastfeeding and Formula Both Feed a Baby Well
related.hook: Health bodies recommend breastfeeding where possible, but properly prepared infant formula is a safe, nourishing alternative — a fed baby is the goal.

related.title: Preparing Formula Safely
related.hook: Powdered formula isn't sterile, so safe prep is about hygiene and getting the ratio exactly right — clean hands and equipment, the correct water-to-powder mix, and fresh feeds made one at a time.

flashcards.prompt: What's an easy rule of thumb for storing freshly expressed breast milk?

choices.text: About 4 hours at room temp, 4 days in the fridge, up to 6 months in the freezer
It keeps for a week at room temperature
It must be used within 1 hour or thrown out

flashcards.explanation_html: A common guideline is roughly 4 hours at room temperature, 4 days refrigerated, and up to 6 months (best) frozen. Label and use the oldest milk first.

flashcards.prompt: How should you thaw and warm stored breast milk?
flashcards.back_html: In the fridge or under warm running water — never the microwave (hot spots). Swirl, don't shake, and don't refreeze milk once thawed.
